chunks: And in the narration of Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
For a finger, there are ten camels if it is cut off from its base or becomes paralyzed.

key_terms.شُلَّتْ: became paralyzed or disabled in function
key_terms.عَشْرٌ مِنَ ٱلْإِبِلِ: ten camels, the prescribed amount of blood money
key_terms.مِنْ أَصْلِهَا: from its base or root, meaning severed completely from the origin
key_terms.ٱلْإِصْبَعِ: the finger, the injured limb under discussion

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for a finger if it is cut off or becomes paralyzed in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on blood money for injury to a finger. It states that the compensation is ten camels when the finger is severed from its root or rendered paralyzed, showing the fixed valuation assigned in fiqh to this bodily injury.
